# Private voice dictation on Mac: the complete guide

We dictate more and more: specs, emails, notes, messages. But almost nobody asks the real question: where does my voice go when I talk to my dictation app?

For most dictation tools, the answer is simple and uncomfortable: your audio ships to their servers, every sentence. For a lawyer, a doctor, a journalist, or a founder dictating something sensitive, that's not a detail. That's the whole story.

Verba takes the problem from the other end. By default, your voice never leaves your Mac.

## What "on-device" actually means
Transcription runs locally, on your Apple Silicon chip, through Verba's own private AI models. No audio upload: only the final text can sync, if you turn that on. Your history is local, with a real off switch and auto-prune, you decide what stays. Your keys live in the macOS Keychain, never a plain file.

## A simple test for your own app
Turn off Wi-Fi and dictate. If transcription stops, your audio was being sent to a server the whole time. Verba keeps going: the engine lives on your machine.

## What about when AI cleans up your text?
Verba restructures your ramble into clean, structured text using its own private AI, built into the app. No server call, no upload, the cleanup happens on your Mac exactly like the transcription.

## Even the agent stays private
When JARVIS acts on what you say (create an issue, draft an email), the plan is generated on your Mac, by your own AI, never a server key. And nothing executes without your confirmation.

Private by default isn't a checkbox. It's how it's built.

→ verba.run

# JARVIS for Mac: the voice that acts, explained

For ten years we've been promised a voice assistant that actually does things. Siri promised us Jarvis. We got a timer and the weather.

The problem was never understanding your sentence. The problem is trust: giving an assistant access to your email, your Slack, your Linear, and letting it act. Too much risk, not enough control.

Verba takes on the trust problem, not the magic trick.

## How JARVIS acts
You talk. JARVIS generates an action plan, on your Mac, with your AI. It shows you exactly what it plans to do: "Create the Linear issue," "Send the team recap." Nothing moves until you confirm.

## Why the Confirm button changes everything
An agent that's actually useful at work can't be one that improvises inside your tools. Verba's framework is simple: reads can run on their own, writes are always confirmed. Nothing executes behind your back.

## Generated on your machine
The plan isn't computed by a key on our server. It's produced by your own AI, on your Mac, we even tested it with our server key empty: it still plans, locally. Your intent isn't ours to keep.

## 1,000+ connected apps
Gmail, Slack, Linear, Calendar, and plenty more. Connect what you want, disconnect whenever you want.

Your voice shouldn't just write. It should act, when you say so, and only then.

→ verba.run

What if you dictated your prompts instead of typing them?

Out loud, your specs come out longer and clearer. You explain the edge cases you usually skip because typing them is a pain. A 20-minute brain-dump becomes a complete PR description, without touching the keyboard.

## The setup, in practice
1. Verba lives in your menu bar. You press a key, you talk.
2. Transcription happens on-device with Verba's own private AI, your audio never leaves your Mac.
3. That same private AI cleans the ramble into a structured, polished prompt, and pastes it straight into Cursor or your coding assistant.
4. The key part: nothing to configure. No account to link, no extra step, no usage dashboard to babysit.

## And when you're ready to act
Dictating the prompt is step one. Step two: "create the Linear issue for this bug and assign it." Verba plans the action on your Mac, shows it to you, and runs it on your confirm. Your flow never leaves your voice.

You code with AI? Try a week without the keyboard.
